faq.q: Which conversions and tools does it include?
faq.a: Seven tabs: a Base Converter (binary, octal, decimal, hex plus any custom base 2–36), a Bit Visualiser with two's complement, Bitwise Operations, Fractional base conversion, Text/ASCII/Unicode, IEEE 754 float breakdown, and Roman numerals. The base fields update live as you type, and a step-by-step working panel shows the repeated-division method into any target base.

faq.q: Can it handle very large numbers without rounding errors?
faq.a: Yes. The base converter uses JavaScript BigInt for integer work, so arbitrarily large whole numbers stay exact rather than losing precision. Negative numbers are supported too. The fractional tab also uses BigInt as an exact rational to generate fractional digits by repeated multiplication, with a precision setting of up to 64 fractional digits.

faq.q: What does the bit visualiser show?
faq.a: Enter a decimal value and choose 8, 16, 32 or 64-bit width. It draws each bit as a clickable box — click to toggle it and the value updates — with the sign bit highlighted. It also displays the unsigned decimal, signed decimal, hex, and the two's complement binary. The Bitwise tab computes AND, OR, XOR, NOT, left shift, logical right shift and arithmetic right shift within the chosen width.

faq.q: Does it convert text and show floating-point internals?
faq.a: Yes. The Text tab converts between text, space-separated binary, hex and Unicode code points in either direction. The IEEE 754 tab breaks a decimal number into sign, exponent (with bias) and mantissa for 32-bit single or 64-bit double, shown as a colour-coded bit grid plus the hex. Roman numeral conversion covers 1 to 3999. A history of the last 20 conversions is kept in localStorage under ncHistory.
